dossier.public_summary: The 13.3-day dip varies far too much to be a planet. One of the five transits is undetectable at 25 ppm and another is more than twice the average at 7352 ppm, and the depth jumps from ~0 to ~7000 ppm between sectors even within the same pipeline. The star is an active M-dwarf whose spin period at 4.4 days is a third of the dip period ([3x]), pointing to spots or a blended eclipsing binary rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by orders of magnitude on short, well-sampled, same-sector timescales; a planet on the target must have a steady depth after dilution. Primary sector 92 and the two later transits agree with the deep dip, sector 42 is consistent with no dip.
Five individual transits are wildly inconsistent; the deepest one and the two close-to-deep ones carry most of the signal.
